**Wire verb `genes resolve`**: Resolve every protein in the given databases to stable Ensembl gene ids, counted against a caller-supplied, release-pinned gene set, with one outcome per protein and the hash of every input.

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `databases` (wire `--path`) | `path` | absent | — | — | One search database (UniProt XML for real answers; a FASTA carries no gene links). Exactly one of path and paths-stdin. |
| `contaminants` (wire `--contaminant`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Load the --path database as contaminants: every protein is contaminant\_not\_mapped. |
| wire `--paths-stdin` | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Databases on stdin, one per line, optionally followed by a tab and 'contaminant' or 'target' (BULK.md §1). |
| `gtf` (wire `--gtf`) | `path` | absent | — | — | An Ensembl GTF, plain or .gz; only gene rows are read. Use the primary-assembly GTF (Species.Assembly.Release.gtf.gz) and keep Ensembl's file name, which carries the release. Exactly one of gtf and gene-set; there is no default. |
| `gene_set` (wire `--gene-set`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Instead of gtf: a compact gene table from mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter. It carries the GTF's provenance, so rows are keyed as against the GTF (tested byte-identical). |
| `xref` (wire `--xref`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Optional Ensembl Species.Assembly.Release.uniprot.tsv(.gz): per-row agreement, and a row per gene only Ensembl links (source ensembl\_xref). |
| `threads` (wire `--threads`) | `int` | `1` | — | `>= 1, or -1 for every core` | Databases loaded (and hashed) at once. Output identical at any value. |
| `on_error` (wire `--on-error`) | `string` | `fail` | — | `fail \| skip` | As proteins read. |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file_count` | `int` | files | never | Databases given. |
| `read_count` | `int` | files | never | Databases read. |
| `failed_count` | `int` | files | never | Databases that failed (on-error skip only). |
| `protein_count` | `int` | proteins | never | Proteins resolved. |
| `record_count` | `int` | rows | never | Rows in columns: at least one per protein; one per gene for multi\_gene; plus ensembl\_xref rows. |
| `gene_set` | `object` | — | never | {source\_file\_name, sha256 (of the file's bytes as read: compressed for .gz), release (null: not in the file name), genome\_build (null: no \#!genome-build header), genebuild\_last\_updated (null: no header), gene\_count}. |
| `xref` | `object` | — | yes: no --xref was given | {source\_file\_name, sha256, release (nullable), accession\_count}. |
| `outcome_counts` | `map<string,int>` | proteins | never | Outcome name -&gt; proteins with it; all six keys always present. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | FASTA proteins (all not\_in\_source), a GTF with no release or genome build, no xref (agreement unknown, not false). |
| `files` | `object[]` | — | never | As proteins read; search\_database\_sha256 is set: lower-case hex sha256 of the DECOMPRESSED database, so .xml and .xml.gz agree. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | source\_index, source\_path, then mzLib's GeneResolutionTsv.Schema headers in its order (a bridge test holds them equal). |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | Column name to per-row values. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_index` | `int` | — | never | Input position. |
| `source_path` | `string` | — | never | Input path. |
| `accession` | `string` | — | never | Verbatim, as the search reported it (a variant suffix kept). |
| `entry_accession` | `string` | — | never | UniProt entry or unversioned RefSeq accession; verbatim when unrecognized. |
| `isoform` | `int` | — | yes: no -N isoform suffix | UniProt isoform number. |
| `namespace` | `string` | — | never | uniprot \| refseq \| unrecognized. |
| `outcome` | `string` | — | never | resolved \| multi\_gene \| off\_primary\_only \| not\_in\_source \| unrecognized\_accession \| contaminant\_not\_mapped (GeneResolutionTsv.OutcomeName). |
| `n_genes` | `int` | genes | never | Genes the search database links on the gene set's assembly. |
| `gene_id` | `string` | — | yes: the outcome has no gene on the assembly | Stable Ensembl gene id. |
| `versioned_gene_id` | `string` | — | yes: no gene on the row | As the database wrote it (e.g. ENSG00000111640.15); for an ensembl\_xref row, built from the GTF's version, or null when the GTF has none. |
| `gene_symbol` | `string` | — | yes: no gene on the row, or the GTF gives it no gene\_name | The release's gene\_name: a display label, never a key. |
| `gene_biotype` | `string` | — | yes: no gene on the row | The release's gene\_biotype ('unknown' when the GTF omits it). |
| `off_primary_genes` | `int` | genes | never | Linked genes outside the gene set (ALT haplotypes, patches, scaffolds): dropped from n\_genes, counted here. |
| `uniprot_gene_name` | `string` | — | yes: the entry names no primary gene | The database's primary gene name, as a label. |
| `source` | `string` | — | never | search\_database\_dbreference, or ensembl\_xref for a gene only Ensembl links (it carries the search database's outcome and never changes it). |
| `search_database_sha256` | `string` | — | never | sha256 of the decompressed database. |
| `gene_set_release` | `string` | — | yes: the GTF's file name carries no release | Ensembl release. |
| `gene_set_sha256` | `string` | — | never | sha256 of the GTF as read. |
| `ensembl_xref_agrees` | `bool` | — | yes: no gene on the row, or no --xref: unknown, not false | Whether Ensembl's xref links this accession to this gene. |
| `ensembl_xref_info_type` | `string` | — | yes: Ensembl's xref does not link the pair, or no --xref | Ensembl's strongest evidence: DIRECT, SEQUENCE\_MATCH, INFERRED\_PAIR. |
| `ensembl_xref_sha256` | `string` | — | yes: no --xref was given | sha256 of the xref file. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | neither or both of gtf and gene-set; a missing GTF, gene set or xref; any database-selection error proteins read raises |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | a GTF gene row without gene\_id (InvalidDataException); an xref whose header is not Ensembl's nine columns; a compact gene table mzLib's reader refuses; a database mzLib cannot parse |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- The caller supplies and pins the gene set. Use the primary-assembly GTF, not chr\_patch\_hapl\_scaff: counting ALT haplotypes as genes made human release 116 look 6.99% multi-gene when it is 0.36% (mzLib EnsemblGeneSet remarks).
- A FASTA carries no Ensembl links, so every FASTA protein is not\_in\_source regardless of biology; the result caveats count them.
- Contaminants are never mapped (contaminant\_not\_mapped), even when they would resolve.
- multi\_gene is one row per gene, never a pick.
